title: WGSL kernels from IR builds
summary: Gives a printed WGSL kernel its meaning through a parser proved to invert the printer, defines the invocation and dispatch semantics of the device model, translates the element of an IR build into WGSL with a simulation lemma from a memory-free denotation, and proves a build kernel from the element lemma its Wasm proof uses.
premises: The device model of 2026-10-04: IEEE32 binary32 results with the canonical NaN, race-free dispatch, the host's length word, a dispatch that covers the count, and no dynamic errors
One buffer per IR parameter: an array's Wasm array, or a scalar's two words, with arrays below 2^29 elements
result: The dispatch leaves the output holding the Lean function's build as a Wasm array, distinct invocations store to distinct words, and the printed text parses to the kernel; the Wasm theorem of the same function follows from the same element lemma.
